text:
alex: Quick sync — thinking about a "grace intent" for automatic degrade policies. Instead of an immediate mode flip on a single spike, we add a brief grace window that samples and routes a small % to degrade for verification before full roll. thoughts?
maria: love the idea. product-wise we want observable checkpoints during the grace window: why it started, sample rate, success metric. can we show that in the console? :eyes:
sam: operationally we need: 1) explicit triggers (5xx spike, latency p95) 2) minimum sampling floor (so we don’t route 0) 3) auto-escalate if errors continue. also need traceIDs passed through for forensics.
lee: console UX notes — show a compact timeline strip for the grace window with three overlays: trigger signal, sample traffic %, and pass/fail metric (e.g., error-rate). clicking the strip expands an audit pane with sampled request ids and a quick-replay button.
alex: agree. propose sample flow: start 1% for 30s, if OK -> 10% for 2m, if OK -> full degrade. if error rate climbs during any step -> rollback and flag operator inbox. thoughts on steps?
maria: ramp plan is good. can we make steps editable in policy editor? Default presets for latency vs error-triggered policies. also want a dry-run toggle that shows simulated impact without routing live requests.
sam: implementation caveat — need to avoid oscillation. add hysteresis: once a policy engages, block re-engagement for X minutes unless manual override. also limit concurrent grace windows per service to avoid confusion.
lee: UX for operator inbox — it should be a single-threaded card per event with actions: approve ramp, abort, annotate (reason), and attach playbook link. show the sampled request examples inline (redactable PII).
alex: on telemetry: add a short lived sampling stream of full KV traces during the grace window that gets tagged with policy_id and step. retention short-lived (72h) plus export to forensic logs if operator marks it. good?
deploy-bot: Simulation complete for service=nlp-embed, policy=grace-intent-v1 -> initial 1% for 30s: errors 0.2% (baseline 0.15%), latency +4ms. No auto-escalation. run_id=sim-2024-05-17-08
maria: nice — can we show the sim results in-policy editor as a preview? that'd help product and SRE signoff.
sam: also add an emergency escape route: if we hit a severe error class (e.g., GPU OOMs, auth 401 storms), the degrade should immediately stop and notify on-call channel. differentiate recoverable vs unrecoverable error triggers.
lee: UI affordance: a tiny inline badge next to policy name showing current state: idle / grace-step-1 / ramping / degraded / paused. clicking opens the operator card. also add emoji reactions for quick ack from SRE (:white_check_mark:, :rotating_light:).
alex: final open question — audit linkage. every change, simulation run, and operator action must create an immutable audit event tied to rollout_id and retrievable by trace id. we should store a short human summary + machine payload. retention policy? compliance might want 1y, but storage cost. propose 90d by default, 1y enterprise option.
maria: fine by product. let's prototype 90d default. add a checkbox for enterprise to flip 1y.
sam: ok — I'll draft the required telemetry events and error classes. alex/lee/maria, can you review the schema I post?
alex: yep. thanks. I'll add the ramp presets and a doc blurb for ops playbook.
lee: I'll mock the operator card and badge states and post screenshots in the thread.
deploy-bot: Note: policy-grace-intent-v1 deployed to staging console flag=on. preview links: https://console.staging/redwood/policies/sim/grace-intent-v1
